newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's imported car sales jump ahead of tax.
newsitem.headline: Japan's imported car sales jump ahead of tax.

text.p: Strong demand for cars ahead of an increase in Japan's national sales tax pushed up sales of imported vehicles last month, but U.S. carmakers experienced a slump in sales, according to figures released Friday.
The Japan Automobile Importers Association said sales of imported vehicles rose 12.7 percent to 57,840 units from a March record of 51,342 last year.
Japan raised the consumption tax to 5 percent Tuesday from 3 percent.
For the fiscal year that ended March 31, imported vehicle sales rose 8.8 percent to a record 437,886 units, the automobile association said.
Most European carmakers, such as Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Adam Opel, Peugeot and Volvo, saw their highest sales ever for March, the group said.
But sales of U.S.-made vehicles fell 34.8 percent to 11,830, due mainly to poor sales of Fords and Japanese maker's U.S.-made cars.

"Japanese consumers' taste is shifting to compact cars so that bulky American cars and off-road type cars are likely to become out-of-date here," Kunihiko Ono, an official of the car trade group, said. Such large vehicles had been popular here in recent years.

A recent survey by the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association said Japanese demand for compact cars was expected to rise due to an increase in buying by women and elderly people, who prefer small cars that are easy to manoeuvre.
